mainTopic: How רבי יוחנן uses ״אֹתָם״ to forbid a voluntary שתי הלחם; whether the ban on burning leftovers covers anything called a קרבן; and how much שאור the ban on burning covers.
overview: The amud opens by asking what רבי יוחנן learns from the word ״אֹתָם״. A ברייתא shows that no one, not a יחיד and not even the ציבור, may donate a voluntary copy of the שתי הלחם. Only the required שתי הלחם (from leaven) and ביכורים (from sweet fruit) are brought. The גמרא challenges this from a ברייתא saying leaven was 'allowed' in the מקדש. רב עמרם answers that this means the loaves are brought together with the lambs, and the גמרא explains why the birds on the ביכורים baskets do not do the same for honey. Next, רמי בר חמא asks whether putting meat of a חטאת העוף on the מזבח breaks the ban on burning leftovers. רב חסדא says yes, because it is called a קרבן, and the גמרא links this to a dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא, with רב חסדא and רב each giving a case where they differ. Finally, a ברייתא widens the ban on burning שאור to part of it and to a mixture. אביי and רבא explain 'part of it' differently, and the root of their dispute about the size of a קומץ begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does רבי יוחנן learn from the word 'them'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן does with the word ״אֹתָם״, since he does not use it the way רבי אלעזר does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן: what does he do with this word 'them'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a standard question. If רבי יוחנן does not use ״אֹתָם״ to limit the ramp prohibition, what does that word teach him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר learned from ״אֹתָם״ that only שתי הלחם and ביכורים are included in the prohibition of bringing them to the ramp. רבי יוחנן says the prohibition covers everything in the list. Since no word in the תורה is extra, the word must teach him something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? This asks what a sage learns from a word he does not use the other way.
'Them,' a word in ויקרא 2:12

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that every word of the פסוק must teach something. It is why רבי יוחנן needs another use for ״אֹתָם״.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan,
this word 'them,' what does he do with it?
phrases.notes: The word is from ויקרא 2:12, 'As an offering of first produce you may bring them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the earlier dispute, where רבי אלעזר used ״אֹתָם״ to limit the ramp prohibition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יוחנן learns from the word ״אֹתָם״.

steps.title: He needs it for a ברייתא: could an individual donate two loaves?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן needs ״אֹתָם״ for a ברייתא. The ברייתא opens by suggesting that an individual might donate an offering like the שתי הלחם as a voluntary gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא: You might think an individual may donate and bring a gift offering like the two loaves. I would apply to it the פסוק 'What comes out of your lips you shall keep and do.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן uses ״אֹתָם״ for a ברייתא. This line opens the ברייתא with a first guess that it will soon reject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guess is that a private person could promise a voluntary offering of two loaves, like the community's שתי הלחם. The support for the guess is the general rule that a promise to bring an offering must be kept. The ברייתא is setting up a question that the next step answers.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (the word) for another teaching
'You might have thought.' It introduces a wrong first guess.
An individual, a private person
A voluntary gift offering
'What comes out of your lips.' The duty to keep a vow.

phrases.english: He needs it for that which is taught in a ברייתא:
One might think that an individual may donate
and bring a gift offering like it,
phrases.notes: 'Like it' means like the community's two loaves, the שתי הלחם.

phrases.english: and I would read concerning it
'That which has gone out of your lips you shall observe and do'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by bringing a ברייתא and starting its first guess.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן uses ״אֹתָם״ for the ברייתא about donating offerings like the שתי הלחם.

steps.title: The plural 'you shall bring' means only the community
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the first guess. ״תַּקְרִיבוּ״ is plural and speaks to the community, so an individual may not bring such an offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'As an offering of first produce you shall bring.' I told you the community may, and not an individual.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own guess with a פסוק. Bringing this kind of offering is for the ציבור, not for a יחיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״תַּקְרִיבוּ״, 'you shall bring,' is in the plural. That shows the offering of first produce belongs to the community as a group. So a private person cannot use the vow rule to donate two loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches.' It introduces the proof from a פסוק.
An offering of first produce
The community

phrases.english: The verse states: 'As an offering of first produce you shall bring,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:12. The point is that 'you shall bring' is plural.

phrases.english: I said to you a community, and not an individual.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first guess of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual may not donate an offering like the שתי הלחם.

steps.title: Maybe the community may donate extra loaves
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא makes a second guess. Maybe only an individual is excluded, because he never brings two loaves as a required offering. The community does bring them as a requirement, so maybe it may donate extra ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that only an individual may not bring them, since he does not bring his required offering in this form. But the community should be able to bring them, since it does bring its required offering in this form?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new guess. Perhaps the community, which already brings two loaves as a requirement, may also bring them as a voluntary gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning compares the two. An individual has no required offering of two loaves, so it makes sense that he cannot donate one. The community does have that requirement, so maybe it can add a voluntary one. The next step will answer this.

keyTerms.meaning: His required (obligatory) offering
Like it, in the same form

phrases.english: One might think an individual may not bring,
since he does not bring his obligatory offering like it,
but the community may bring,
since it does bring its obligatory offering like it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 3's exclusion of the individual and suggests the community might be different.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that only the individual is excluded from donating two loaves.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The community already brings two loaves as a requirement, so perhaps it may also donate them voluntarily.

steps.title: 'Them' excludes everyone: only the required loaves and first fruits
steps.stepSummary: ״אֹתָם״ rules out a voluntary offering of two loaves even for the community. The only offerings ever brought from leaven and honey are the שתי הלחם and the ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'them.' What is left for you to bring? The two loaves from leaven, and the first fruits from honey.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes with the word ״אֹתָם״. Only 'them,' the required שתי הלחם and the ביכורים, are brought. Nobody, not even the community, may donate extra loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אֹתָם״ limits the offering to exactly the ones the תורה requires. That shuts down the community's voluntary gift too. This answers the opening question: this is what רבי יוחנן learns from ״אֹתָם״.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves brought on שבועות
Leaven
First fruits
Honey. Here it means sweet fruit.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן uses ״אֹתָם״ to teach that no voluntary שתי הלחם may be brought, by an individual or by the community. Only the required שתי הלחם (leaven) and ביכורים (sweet fruit) are brought.
steps.confusionAlert: Here ״דבש״ does not mean bee honey. It means sweet fruit, which is what ביכורים are.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'them,'
And what is there for you to bring?
The two loaves from leaven,
and first fruits from honey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second guess and completes the answer to step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״אֹתָם״ teaches רבי יוחנן that no one may donate a voluntary שתי הלחם. Only the required שתי הלחם and ביכורים are brought.

steps.title: Challenge: Can't the two loaves be brought as a gift?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the conclusion that the שתי הלחם may never be a voluntary offering. It brings a ברייתא that asks why the פסוק says both ״כׇּל שְׂאֹר״ and ״כׇּל דְּבַשׁ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that the two loaves can't be brought as a gift? But a ברייתא teaches: if the פסוק says 'any leaven,' why does it also need 'any honey'? And if it says 'any honey,' why does it also need 'any leaven'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge to the conclusion of Step 5 by quoting a ברייתא. This step is setup: the actual contradiction only comes out in Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about ויקרא 2:11, which forbids burning leaven and honey on the מזבח. It asks why both items need the extra word ״כׇּל״, since you might think one could be learned from the other. The answer to that question will hold the material the גמרא uses to attack.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaven, the sourdough used to make bread rise; it stands for anything חמץ
Honey, which here includes sweet fruit syrups
A voluntary offering, brought by choice and not as an obligation

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'why do we need both' is the ברייתא's own question. It is not yet the גמרא's attack. The attack comes later, in Step 10.

phrases.english: And may the two loaves not be brought as a gift offering?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
If it says 'any leaven,'
why does it say 'any honey'?
And if it says 'any honey,'
why does it say 'any leaven'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם לֹא יִקְרְבוּ נְדָבָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 5 by bringing a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling from ״אֹתָם״ that the community may not bring the שתי הלחם as a gift
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about leaven and honey will suggest that leaven was allowed on the מזבח through a gift of two loaves

steps.title: Each of leaven and honey has its own special rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers its question in general terms: leaven has a feature honey lacks, and honey has a feature leaven lacks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there is something true of leaven that isn't true of honey, and something true of honey that isn't true of leaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the general reason both words are needed. The details come in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two things each have a different special feature, you can't learn one from the other. So the תורה must state each one on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is not': a feature one item has and the other lacks

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּשְּׂאוֹר מַה שֶּׁאֵין בַּדְּבַשׁ,
phrases.english: Because there is in leaven what is not in honey,
and there is in honey what is not in leaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּשְּׂאוֹר מַה שֶּׁאֵין בַּדְּבַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from Step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both words are needed because each item has a unique feature, so neither can be learned from the other

steps.title: Leaven's special feature: it was allowed in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: Leaven was allowed in some way in the מקדש, even though its general rule forbids it. Honey was never allowed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Leaven was allowed out of its general rule in the מקדש; honey was not allowed out of its general rule in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains what leaven has that honey does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaven is usually forbidden for offerings, yet some leavened items were used in the מקדש. So you might think leaven is a weaker prohibition, and you couldn't learn the full honey prohibition from it. The phrase 'allowed in the מקדש' is exactly what the גמרא will soon examine.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Permitted out of its general rule': an exception was made to a prohibition
The בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is what the גמרא will use to argue that two loaves can be brought as a gift.

phrases.english: Leaven was permitted out of its general rule in the Temple,
honey was not permitted out of its general rule in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first half of the general answer in Step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaven had an exception in the מקדש; honey had none

steps.title: Honey's special feature, and the ברייתא's summary
steps.stepSummary: Honey may be used with the leftover portions of meal offerings, but leaven may not. So both ״כׇּל שְׂאֹר״ and ״כׇּל דְּבַשׁ״ are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Honey was allowed with the leftovers of meal offerings; leaven was not allowed with the leftovers of meal offerings. So, since each has something the other lacks, the פסוק had to say 'any leaven' and also 'any honey.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives honey's special feature and then wraps up its answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים may eat their leftover part of a מנחה with honey, but they may not let it become leavened. Honey is weaker in this way, and leaven was weaker in the מקדש. Since each one is lenient somewhere, neither can be learned from the other, and both words are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftovers of a מנחה that the כהנים eat after the handful is burned
'It was necessary to say': the פסוק had to state it

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא: leaven had an exception in the מקדש, and honey had an exception in the שיירי מנחות. So both words in the פסוק are needed.

phrases.english: Honey was permitted in the remainders of meal offerings,
leaven was not permitted in the remainders of meal offerings.

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּשְּׂאוֹר מַה שֶּׁאֵין בַּדְּבַשׁ,
phrases.english: So, because there is in leaven what is not in honey,
and there is in honey what is not in leaven,
it was necessary to say 'any leaven,'
and it was necessary to say 'any honey.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second half of the answer and closes the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Honey is allowed with the שיירי מנחות and leaven is not, so both words in the פסוק are needed

steps.title: The attack: 'allowed in the מקדש' must mean two loaves as a gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case the ברייתא means by 'leaven was allowed in the מקדש'. It suggests this means the two loaves offered as a gift, which would contradict Step 5.
steps.simpleTranslation: Leaven that was allowed out of its general rule in the מקדש: what is that? Isn't it that two loaves may be offered as a gift?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא makes its actual challenge. It reads the ברייתא as saying leaven can go on the מזבח when the two loaves are brought as a voluntary offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The required שתי הלחם never go on the מזבח, so they don't count as leaven 'allowed' for the מזבח. The גמרא reasons that the exception must be a voluntary gift of two loaves that is offered on the מזבח. That directly clashes with ״אֹתָם״, which ruled out such a gift.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is it?': asking which case is meant
'Isn't it...?': a question that expects a yes

phrases.english: Leaven that was permitted out of its general rule in the Temple,
what is it?
Isn't it the two loaves, which are offered as a gift?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׂאוֹר דְּהוּתַּר מִכְּלָלוֹ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, מַאי נִיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the line in Step 8 to complete the challenge begun in Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion from ״אֹתָם״ that the שתי הלחם can never be a voluntary gift
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's exception for leaven seems to refer to a gift of two loaves placed on the מזבח, so such a gift must be allowed

steps.title: רב עמרם: the leaven is brought together with the lambs
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם says the exception doesn't mean a gift of two loaves. It means the leavened loaves are brought together with the lambs as one offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said: No. It means the loaves are offered together with them, with the lambs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא's exception differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The required שתי הלחם come together with the two lambs (the כבשי עצרת), and the lambs do go on the מזבח. Since they form one offering, the leaven counts as 'allowed in the מקדש' through them. There is no need for a voluntary two-loaf gift, so ״אֹתָם״ still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'With them': together with the two lambs
The two lambs (שלמים) brought on שבועות together with the שתי הלחם

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge falls away. Leaven's exception in the מקדש is the required שתי הלחם brought with the lambs, not a voluntary gift. So ״אֹתָם״ still rules out a gift of two loaves.

phrases.english: Rav Amram said:
No, it means they are brought with them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the two lambs of שבועות; the loaves are part of their offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם: לָא, לִיקְרַב עִמָּהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'leaven allowed in the מקדש' means a voluntary gift of two loaves on the מזבח
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the required שתי הלחם brought together with the lambs, so a voluntary gift is still forbidden

steps.title: Then honey was also allowed, through first fruits
steps.stepSummary: If leavened loaves count as an exception because they come with the lambs, then ביכורים should also count as an exception for honey, since they come with birds that are offered as עולות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is so, the same should be true of first fruits. We learned in a משנה: the young birds placed on top of the baskets were offered as burnt offerings, and the baskets the people held were given to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב עמרם's answer from Step 11 by applying the same logic to ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב עמרם said leaven counts as 'allowed' because the leavened loaves are brought together with the lambs as one offering. ביכורים, which can include honey-sweet fruit, are brought together with birds that become עולות. By the same logic, honey would also have been 'allowed' in the מקדש, which goes against the ברייתא's claim in Step 8 that honey never was.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if your answer is right, then...
First fruits brought to the מקדש
Young birds, fledglings
Baskets holding the first fruits
Burnt offerings, burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: If so, first fruits too should count,
phrases.notes: He means: by רב עמרם's logic, ביכורים would make honey 'allowed' in the מקדש, just as the two loaves did for leaven.

phrases.english: as we learned in a משנה:
the young birds that were on top of the baskets
were offered as burnt offerings,
and the baskets that were in their hands
are given to the כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב עמרם's answer by applying its logic to a parallel case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב עמרם's explanation that leaven counts as allowed because the loaves come together with the lambs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If coming together with a real קרבן makes something count as offered, then ביכורים coming with birds that become עולות would make honey count as allowed, which contradicts the ברייתא.

steps.title: The birds were only decoration
steps.stepSummary: The birds on the baskets are not part of the ביכורים offering. They only came to decorate the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those birds only came to decorate the first fruits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the birds and the ביכורים are not one joined offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lambs and the two loaves are truly brought together as one offering. The birds on the ביכורים baskets are only there to make the fruit look nice, even though they end up as עולות. So the ביכורים are not tied to a real קרבן, and honey was never 'allowed' in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: To decorate, to beautify

steps.whatToRemember: Leaven has an exception (the two loaves with the lambs). Honey has none, because the birds on the ביכורים are only decoration.

phrases.english: Those birds were to decorate the first fruits,
that is why they came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the birds are decoration, not a joined offering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The birds and ביכורים are one offering, like the lambs and loaves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The birds only decorate the ביכורים, so honey was never allowed in the מקדש.

steps.title: Putting meat of a bird sin offering on the altar
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא: if someone puts meat of a חטאת העוף on the מזבח, is he breaking the ban on burning leftovers?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked רב חסדא: someone who puts some meat of a bird sin offering on the altar, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רמי בר חמא asks about burning meat of a bird חטאת, which is meant to be eaten by the כהנים, on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban 'do not burn' also covers leftover parts of קרבנות, which are not supposed to go on the מזבח. A חטאת העוף is unusual: none of it is burned on the מזבח at all. So it is unclear whether the ban applies to its meat.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a real question, unsure of the answer
A bird brought as a sin offering; its meat is eaten by the כהנים
One who brings up (onto the מזבח)
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: רמי בר חמא asked רב חסדא:
one who brings up some meat of a bird sin offering
onto the altar, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He is asking whether this person breaks the ban 'do not burn' and gets מלקות.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the ban on burning leftovers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does putting meat of a חטאת העוף on the מזבח break the ban on burning leftovers?

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the doubt: is the ban limited to things part of which went into the fire, or does it cover anything called a קרבן?
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה said the ban covers anything part of which goes into the fire, and none of this bird goes into the fire? Or perhaps it covers anything called an offering, and this bird is also called an offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is hard by laying out two ways to define the ban. This sets up רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the ban covers only an item part of which was burned on the מזבח, and a חטאת העוף has no burned part, so there is no violation. Side two: the ban covers anything with the name קרבן, and a חטאת העוף is a קרבן, so there is a violation.

keyTerms.meaning: The fires of the מזבח
Anything part of which goes to the fire
Anything that has the name 'offering'
Or perhaps

phrases.english: The Merciful One said 'anything part of which goes to the fire,'
phrases.notes: This rule comes from the words 'ממנו... אשה' in the פסוק about not burning, ויקרא 2:11.

phrases.english: and none of this one goes to the fire?
Or perhaps it means anything called an offering,
and this one is also called an offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two possible sides of the question in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the ban defined by 'part went to the fire' or by 'called a קרבן'?

steps.title: Anything called an offering is included
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the ban covers anything called a קרבן, so the bird חטאת is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: the ban covers anything called an offering, and this one is also called an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא picks the second side: the bird חטאת is covered by the ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban does not depend on whether part of the animal was burned. It depends on whether the item is a קרבן. Since a חטאת העוף is a קרבן, putting its meat on the מזבח breaks the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought in the מקדש

phrases.english: He said to him: anything called an offering,
and this one is also called an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Steps 14 and 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban covers anything called a קרבן, so one who puts meat of a חטאת העוף on the מזבח is liable.

steps.title: The same question is a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the two sides match a dispute: רבי אליעזר says 'part goes to the fire', and רבי עקיבא says 'called a קרבן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים: רבי אליעזר says the ban covers anything part of which goes to the fire; רבי עקיבא says it covers anything called an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רמי בר חמא's question was already argued about by תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי אליעזר's rule, a חטאת העוף is not included, since none of it is burned. By רבי עקיבא's rule, it is included. רב חסדא's answer matches רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: This matches a dispute between תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to define the ban on burning leftovers: 'part goes to the fire' (רבי אליעזר) or 'called a קרבן' (רבי עקיבא). רב חסדא follows רבי עקיבא, so the bird חטאת is included.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute between תנאים:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ לָאִישִּׁים,
phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says: anything part of which goes to the fire;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ קׇרְבָּן.
phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says: anything called an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the question and answer to an earlier dispute between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two sides of the question match the views of רבי אליעזר ('part goes to the fire') and רבי עקיבא ('called a קרבן').

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two views?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which real case would come out differently under רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has just matched the two sides to a dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא. Now it asks for a real case where they would rule differently. This line sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most things called a קרבן also have some part burned on the מזבח, so both definitions usually give the same result. The גמרא wants a case that is called a קרבן but has nothing burned. Only in such a case do the two views split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? (asks for a practical case where two opinions disagree)

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא from the step just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the dispute identified in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete case where 'part goes to the fire' and 'called a קרבן' give different rulings.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the meat of a bird sin offering
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the difference is the meat of a חטאת העוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The difference between them is the meat of a bird sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the meat of a חטאת העוף is the case where the two views split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No part of a חטאת העוף is burned on the מזבח, but it is still called a קרבן. So רבי עקיבא would say someone who burns its meat breaks the ban, and רבי אליעזר would say he does not. This is the same case רמי בר חמא asked about in Step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: The meat of a bird sin offering, which is eaten by the כהנים and not burned
There is a difference between them

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The meat of a bird sin offering is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בְּשַׂר חַטַּאת הָעוֹף אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The meat of a חטאת העוף: under רבי עקיבא burning it breaks the ban, and under רבי אליעזר it does not.

steps.title: רב: the leper's log of oil
steps.stepSummary: רב gives a different case, the לוג שמן of a מצורע, which the ברייתא of לוי includes as a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The difference between them is the לוג שמן of a מצורע. As לוי teaches: 'Every offering of theirs' comes to include the לוג שמן of a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב offers a second example of a case where the two views split. He uses the לוג שמן that comes with a מצורע's offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי learns from the words 'כל קרבנם' that the מצורע's לוג שמן counts as a קרבן, yet none of it is burned on the מזבח. So it fits רבי עקיבא's definition but not רבי אליעזר's. This makes it another case where burning it would be forbidden according to one view and allowed according to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A log-measure of oil brought with the guilt offering of a recovered leper
A person with צרעת who is now becoming pure
To include (a word in the פסוק adds a case)

phrases.english: Rav said:
The log of oil of a leper
is the difference between them,
as Levi teaches:
'Every offering of theirs'
comes to include the log of oil of a leper.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: לוֹג שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל מְצוֹרָע אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question of Step 18, in place of רב חסדא's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מצורע's לוג שמן is called a קרבן because of לוי's ברייתא, but none of it is burned. So רבי עקיבא would forbid burning it and רבי אליעזר would not.

steps.title: A ברייתא: burning part of the leaven, or leaven mixed into something else
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'כל' that burning part of the שאור is forbidden, and from 'כי כל' that burning a mixture containing it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Leaven ... you shall not burn.' I only know that this applies to all of it. From where do we know it applies to part of it? The verse says 'any.' From where do we know it applies to it when mixed? The verse says 'for any.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic, the ban on burning שאור on the מזבח. It quotes a ברייתא that widens the ban using extra words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the extra words, the ban would only cover burning 'all of it.' The word 'כל' adds burning only 'part of it,' and the longer phrase 'כי כל' adds שאור mixed into something else. The ברייתא does not yet explain what 'all of it' and 'part of it' mean, and that unclear point leads to the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaven, the sourdough starter that makes dough rise
Do not burn it (on the מזבח)
Part of it
Its mixture, when it is mixed into something else
The verse teaches (introduces a word that proves the point)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'Leaven ... you shall not burn'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:11. The dots show the ברייתא is skipping words in the middle of the פסוק.

phrases.english: I only know this about all of it,
from where do we know it applies to part of it?
The verse says: 'any.'
From where do we know it applies to it when mixed?
The verse says: 'for any.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא discussion and returns to the ban on burning שאור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on burning שאור covers part of it (from 'כל') and a mixture containing it (from 'כי כל').

steps.title: What does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by 'all of it' and 'part of it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא actually means. This line sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, 'all of it' is strange. Is someone liable only if he burns the whole lump of שאור? The גמרא needs these words defined as measurements.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? (asks for the meaning of an unclear statement)

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the unclear wording of the ברייתא in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'כולו' and 'מקצתו' in the ברייתא.

steps.title: אביי: 'all of it' means a כזית, and 'part of it' means half a כזית
steps.stepSummary: אביי rereads the ברייתא. The basic ban covers a כזית, 'כל' adds half a כזית, and 'כי כל' adds a mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, this is what it is saying: 'Leaven, do not burn.' I only know this about an olive-bulk. From where do we know it applies to half an olive-bulk? The verse says 'any.' From where do we know it applies to its mixture? The verse says 'for any.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains that the ברייתא is talking about amounts. 'All of it' means a full כזית, and 'part of it' means half a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a person is punished only for a כזית, so the basic פסוק covers a כזית. The word 'כל' extends the ban down to half a כזית. 'כי כל' still adds the case of שאור mixed into something else.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (introduces a reworded explanation)
An olive-bulk, the standard minimum amount in many laws
Half an olive-bulk

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on burning שאור on the מזבח covers a כזית, half a כזית (from 'כל'), and שאור mixed into something else (from 'כי כל').
steps.confusionAlert: 'All of it' does not mean the whole lump of dough. אביי explains it as a full כזית, the normal amount for punishment.

phrases.english: Abaye said, this is what it is saying:
'Leaven, do not burn'
I only know this about an olive-bulk,
from where do we know it applies to half an olive-bulk?
The verse says 'any,'
from where do we know it applies to its mixture?
The verse says 'for any.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 22 by rereading the ברייתא's terms as amounts.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כולו' means a כזית and 'מקצתו' means half a כזית. 'כל' adds half a כזית, and 'כי כל' adds a mixture.

steps.title: רבא reads the ברייתא as whole handful, half handful, and mixture
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the ברייתא differently. The basic ban covers a whole קומץ, 'כל' adds half a קומץ, and 'כי כל' adds a mixture containing שאור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what the ברייתא means. From 'Do not burn leaven' I only know about a whole handful. How do I know about half a handful? The verse says 'any.' How do I know about its mixture? The verse says 'as any.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the same question from step 22, what 'all of it' and 'part of it' mean, but he gives a different answer than אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי measured everything in olive sizes: a כזית, then half a כזית. רבא measures in handfuls: a whole קומץ, then half a קומץ. Both agree that 'כי כל' adds a mixture. Only the meaning of the 'whole' and the 'part' changes.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour the כהן takes from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח
Half of that handful
Its mixture, meaning something with שאור mixed into it
The verse teaches, used to bring a source from a פסוק
This is what it means, used to reread a source

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing about the mixture. Both he and אביי agree 'כי כל' adds a mixture. They only disagree about whether the basic unit is an olive size or a handful.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא from step 21. רבא is giving his own reading instead of אביי's.

phrases.english: "Leaven... you shall not burn"
I have only a handful;
from where do we know half a handful?
The verse says: "Any."
From where do we know its mixture?
The verse says: "As any."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question of step 22, parallel to and differing from אביי's answer in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'whole' is a full קומץ and the 'part' is half a קומץ. 'כי כל' adds a mixture.

steps.title: What are אביי and רבא arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle lies behind the difference between אביי's reading and רבא's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks what deeper idea makes אביי speak of olive sizes and רבא speak of handfuls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the two readings look almost the same, so the גמרא wants to know if there is a real difference. The answer will show that they disagree about how small a קומץ can be.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? Used to find the root principle behind two opinions

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two readings just given and asks for the principle that divides them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that explains why אביי and רבא read the ברייתא differently.

steps.title: אביי holds a handful can be smaller than two olives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer. אביי holds that a קומץ can be less than the size of two olives.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי holds: there can be a handful that is less than two olive sizes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering its question by giving אביי's view about the size of a קומץ. רבא's side comes in the next words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a קומץ can be smaller than two olives, then half a קומץ might be smaller than one כזית. That explains why אביי does not speak of 'half a handful' and instead uses fixed olive sizes: a כזית and half a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than the size of two olives
An olive's size, a standard measure in הלכה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the argument is not just about wording. It depends on a real question: how big is a קומץ?

phrases.english: Abaye holds:
There is a handful that is less than two olive sizes,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי סָבַר: יֵשׁ קוֹמֶץ פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנֵי זֵיתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 25 by stating אביי's side of the dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי holds that a קומץ can be less than two olive sizes. רבא's opposing view follows in the next words.
